Works with

Rugged tablet for IBM Maximo Mobile

IBM Maximo Mobile is the mobile client for IBM Maximo Manage within the Maximo Application Suite. IBM describes it as a role-based mobile solution that lets technicians and supervisors manage work and assets from virtually any location, with apps for Technician, Inspections, Approvals, Assets, Inventory Counting, Receiving, Issues and Transfers and Service Requests. IBM's own UK case studies include Transport for London, with roughly 10,000 field technicians on Maximo, and the power generator VPI, which runs Maximo Application Suite across four sites.

On the floor or on site a technician uses the app to pick up assigned work orders, record labour, materials and tools, change status, complete inspection forms, scan bar codes and QR codes with the device camera and, on Android, tap NFC tags on assets or locations to pull up their work orders. IBM documents that the app keeps an encrypted local data store and synchronises automatically when connectivity returns. In practice that means work in plant rooms, tunnels and substations without signal, which is a hard job for a consumer tablet: no ingress rating, a glass back that cracks when dropped on a gantry, a battery that does not last a shift and a screen that does not respond to gloves.

This page lists what IBM publishes about device requirements for Maximo Mobile, maps those requirements to the Tuga A10, Tuga W10 and Tuga A6, and is honest about what is not documented. It is written for maintenance, engineering and facilities managers, and the buyers who provision devices for them, who already run Maximo and need hardware for technicians.

Requirements

What IBM Maximo Mobile needs from a device

Each item below comes from IBM (International Business Machines Corp.)'s own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Platform and minimum operating system

    IBM's device requirements page states the device must have Android version 11 or higher, iOS version 14.3 or higher, or Windows 10 version 10.0.17763.0 or better, or Windows 11 installed. The Google Play listing gives the required Android version as 11 and the Microsoft Store listing gives Windows 10 version 17763.0 or higher on x86 or x64. Source: ibm.com

  • Minimum memory of 3 GB, storage depends on data downloaded

    IBM states the minimum memory required is 3 GB, and that long inspection forms or maps with many records may need more memory and processing power. Storage needed depends on how much data the user downloads for offline use; IBM gives no fixed figure. Source: ibm.com

  • Offline working with encrypted local data and automatic sync

    IBM documents that the app can be used online or offline. A local JSON data store is created on the device and encrypted with a key held in the device keystore. When connectivity is restored, local data is automatically synchronised, and users can also trigger a manual sync. First login requires network connectivity, and some apps, such as Assist and Parts Identifier, require the user to be online. Source: ibm.com

  • Bar code and QR scanning through the device camera

    IBM's Maximo Mobile overview page says the Receiving app can use the device camera to read bar codes and QR codes to find purchase orders. IBM's bar code format support page lists the supported formats per platform (for example QR Code, Data Matrix, Code 128, Code 39, EAN-8, EAN-13 and UPC-A on Android, with PDF417 on Windows). By default the reader tries all formats, and IBM's configuring default bar code formats page describes restricting them through the mxe.barcode.readers setting in each app's configuration. IBM's documentation does not describe dedicated or Bluetooth scanner support for this app. Source: ibm.com

  • NFC tag scanning on Android and iOS

    IBM's What's new in Maximo Mobile 8.11 page says you can use an Android or iOS device to scan asset or location NFC tags to show all the work orders for that asset or location. NFC is not documented for the Windows client. RFID is not documented for Maximo Mobile on the Maximo Application Suite. Source: ibm.com

  • Windows devices need WebView2 Runtime and install from the Microsoft Store or IBM portal

    IBM states that Windows devices must include the WebView2 Runtime. The Windows client is listed on the Microsoft Store as IBM Maximo Mobile, publisher International Business Machines Corp., for Windows 10 version 17763.0 or higher on x86 and x64, last updated 7 October 2026. IBM's device requirements page also mentions download from the IBM portal for Windows. Source: apps.microsoft.com

  • Device security credentials and IBM's accessory guidance for technicians

    IBM's authentication and data flow page says that each time the app opens, users are prompted for their device's security credentials so the app can access the encrypted local data store, whose key is saved in the device keystore. IBM's device requirements page says that for shared devices, PIN and biometrics must be available for authentication on the device. The same page recommends hard cases, screen protectors, and a stylus, rubber pens or touchscreen-sensitive gloves for technicians. IBM publishes no specific device models or screen sizes. Source: ibm.com

Worth knowing. Points to weigh before buying. None of the Tuga devices has a dedicated scan engine that IBM documents for this app: IBM describes bar code and QR scanning through the device camera, and does not describe dedicated or Bluetooth scanner support for Maximo Mobile on the Maximo Application Suite, so the W10's optional 2D barcode scanner should be treated as unverified for this app. RFID, including the W10's optional UHF RFID reader, is not documented by IBM for Maximo Mobile on MAS. IBM documents NFC tag scanning for Android and iOS devices only, so do not rely on NFC with the Windows client on the W10. The Assist app requires an ARCore-supported Android device and an online connection; we have not verified whether any Tuga device is on Google's ARCore list, so do not assume Assist or AR features will work. A user-submitted request on IBM's Ideas portal (August 2026, under review) reports that the Windows client has no in-app zoom for users on rugged Windows tablets; this is a feature request rather than IBM documentation, but it is relevant to the W10's 1280 x 800 display and worth checking on a trial unit. Finally, if your organisation has an Apple device policy (IBM's Transport for London case study describes field staff on iPad and iPhone), Tuga does not sell iOS devices.
Setting up

Getting IBM Maximo Mobile running

  1. Confirm with your Maximo administrator or IBM partner that your organisation has IBM Maximo Application Suite with Maximo Manage and that your technicians have user accounts with the right role-based apps assigned. Maximo Mobile is the client for that deployment, not standalone software.
  2. On a Tuga A10 or A6, install IBM Maximo Mobile from Google Play (package com.ibm.iot.maximo.mobile, published by International Business Machines Corp.). Do not install the separate app called IBM Maximo Mobile for EAM, whose Play listing says it is for a Maximo Asset Management 7.6.1.3 system. On a Tuga W10, install IBM Maximo Mobile from the Microsoft Store, or from the IBM portal if your administrator directs you there, and confirm the WebView2 Runtime is present as IBM requires.
  3. Set a device PIN, fingerprint or face unlock on the tablet before first use. IBM states that users are prompted for their device's security credentials so the app can access the encrypted local data store, and that shared devices must have PIN and biometrics available for authentication.
  4. Connect the device to Wi-Fi or mobile data for first login, since IBM states the first login requires network connectivity, then sign in with your Maximo credentials and allow the initial data download to complete.
  5. Test offline working the way IBM describes it: put the device in flight mode (airplane mode in IBM's wording), open a work order, record an update, then restore connectivity and confirm the change synchronises. Also test camera scanning on an asset bar code and, on the Android devices, an NFC tag if your site uses them.
  6. Fit the tempered glass screen protector and hand strap, and set up the charging dock or vehicle mounting dock so devices return to a known place at shift end.
